newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates up, spots mostly down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates up, spots mostly down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed up across the board on Wednesday boosted by a new A share issue on the Shanghai stock exchange, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract soared to 18.00 percent from 9.99 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market rose sharply to 5.61 million losts from 2.06 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
The new A share issue of Sanxia Shuili on the Shanghai bourse was the major factor tp boost fund demand on the repo market, traders said.
"There was a lack of new A share issue on the Shanghai stock exchange for about three weeks," said one trader. "So this issue had fanned the repo market sentiment."
Both rates and volumes were boosted by the new issue, especially the seven-day contract, said traders.
Traders said they expected the rates to correct on Thursday due to sharp rises on Wednesday.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Wednesday with the new A share issue on the Shanghai bourse sucking some of the short-term funds out of the spot market, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond maturing in June 2006 fell to 111.33 yuan from 111.50 yuan. Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose to 657,112 lots from 549,339 lots.

Traders said prices were likely to remain stable around current levels in the next few days. But they added that if the government quickened the speed of new A shares issues, spot prices would fall due to the outflow of funds.
